Text: Lets players join your games through Steam, and uses Steam to find games in Quick match and Open matches. Off, players join by code or address, and games are found without Steam. On some networks, Steam's peer-to-peer connections don't work or are slower than a direct one.
Let Steam friends join without an invite
Your Steam friends can join your game without an invite, and it's listed in Open matches for anyone, unless you tick "Invite only" when you host. Off, players join only by invite, code or address.
Only play with the exact same build

Turns away players whose BeaverBuddies isn't the exact same build as yours, with the same game version, add-on mods and factions, and keeps you from joining a host whose isn't. Off, you're warned and play on, but the game may fall out of sync. Players on different builds play together only if both the host and the guest have this off.

While you host or play in someone's game, your game keeps running when another app is in front, whatever the game's own "Run in background" says. A host whose game stops stops everyone's; a guest whose game stops falls behind and catches up. Outside multiplayer, the game's own setting applies. Uses more battery on a laptop.

Comment: Followed by one of the values below

Text: How often your game autosaves, by the time that passes, not the game's. For games you host or join, and any game in the Multiplayer settlement; other games autosave every 10 minutes, as the game does.

How many autosaves of a settlement are kept: past that, the oldest is deleted. For games you host or join, and any game in the Multiplayer settlement, where the games you join are all saved and so share these, even one you open alone. Other games keep 3, as the game does.

While the game is paused, an autosave that's due waits until it plays again, so a long pause doesn't fill the autosaves with copies of one moment and push the older ones out. The save made as you leave the game is made anyway. For games you host or join, and any game in the Multiplayer settlement.

What pauses the game for every player in a game you host.

Menu and dialogs: the game's own behavior. Opening the menu pauses everyone, and so do the host's dialogs (deconstruction, research).
Menu only: opening the menu pauses everyone; dialogs don't.
Nothing: each player's menu is their own and pauses nobody.

The pause button and speed keys always pause everyone. Saves always wait for the end of the current tick, so they're consistent either way.
Pause the game while you save

A save you make yourself is written with the game paused, as in a single-player game, and the game then plays on at its speed. Autosaves aren't paused. Either way, guests wait at the same moment while you save.
Play on after a resync or a join

When the game reloads for everyone, after a desync or as a player joins, it plays on at the speed it was at once everyone is back, or after a minute, rather than waiting paused for you to press play. Setting a speed meanwhile cancels it.
